cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Confess First
cards.instruction: Get someone else to confess or incriminate themselves before you reveal anything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Before we plan Mum's apology dinner, why did she spend her birthday outside the restaurant?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I forgot the booking. What happened to her present?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Did you forget, or assume I'd book it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I assumed you'd do it. Now your turn.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Even after telling Mum it was confirmed? Give me that bit, then you get the present.

mechanism: A controls the sequence and adequacy of family confessions, withholding personal disclosure until B admits an increasingly specific fault.
confusable: A reciprocal apology discussion would trade turns; this pair requires A to keep approval of turn-taking and demand B incrimination first.
comparison: The family exchange tests false reassurance to Mum rather than the office alternative warning-label misuse and visible smoke.
seedUse: The existing D16-b question restriction and final condition already merge S01 approval with the confession-first pursuit.
